title.zh: 卷一百五十七 列傳第一百〇七: 王翃 郗士美 李鄘 辛秘 馬摠 韋弘景 王彥威
title.en: Volume 157 Biographies 107: Wang Hong, Chi Shimei, Li Yong, Xinmi, Ma Hui, Wei Hongjing, Wang Yanwei
title.raw: 卷一百五十七 列傳第一百〇七: 王翃 郗士美 李鄘 辛秘 馬摠 韋弘景 王彥威 Volume 157 Biographies 107: Wang Hong, Chi Shimei, Li Yong, Xinmi, Ma Hui, Wei Hongjing, Wang Yanwei

sentences.zh: 王翃，太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Hong was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong came from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 兄翊，乾元中累官至京兆少尹。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yi, during the Qianyuan era, rose through successive posts to Vice Magistrate of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yi, in the Qianyuan period, rose through successive offices to Vice Magistrate of the Capital District.

sentences.zh: 性謙柔，淡於聲利。

translations.literal: His nature was modest and gentle, and he was indifferent to fame and gain.
translations.idiomatic: He was modest and unassuming, and cared little for reputation or profit.

sentences.zh: 自商州刺史遷襄州刺史、山南東道節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: From Prefect of Shang Prefecture he was transferred to Prefect of Xiang Prefecture and Commissioner for Military Affairs and Observation in the Eastern Circuit of Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved from prefect of Shang to prefect of Xiang and commissioner for military affairs and observation in the Eastern Circuit of Shannan.

sentences.zh: 入朝，充北蕃宣慰使，稱職。

translations.literal: He entered court and served as envoy to pacify the northern borderlands, performing his duties well.
translations.idiomatic: On entering court he served as envoy to pacify the northern frontier peoples and acquitted himself well.

sentences.zh: 代宗素重之，及即位，目為純臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong had long valued him, and when he took the throne he regarded him as a pure-hearted minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong had long esteemed him, and when he acceded regarded him as a minister of unblemished loyalty.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部侍郎、御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 居憲司，雖不能舉振綱條，然以謹重知名。

translations.literal: While in the Censorate, though he could not invigorate its regulations, he was known for his prudence and gravity.
translations.idiomatic: Though he could not revitalize the censorial code, he was known in the Censorate for prudence and dignity.

sentences.zh: 大歷二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Dali (767).

sentences.zh: 翊為侍郎時，翃自折沖授辰州刺史，遷朗州，有威望智術，所蒞立名。

translations.literal: When Yi was Vice Minister, Hong was appointed from Commander Who Repels the Enemy to Prefect of Chen Prefecture, then transferred to Lang Prefecture; he possessed prestige, wisdom, and stratagem, and wherever he served he established a name.
translations.idiomatic: While Yi was vice minister, Hong was appointed from Commander Who Repels the Enemy to prefect of Chen, then transferred to Lang; he had authority, wit, and strategy, and everywhere he served he made a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 大歷五年遷容州刺史、容管經略使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dali he was transferred to Prefect of Rong Prefecture and Commissioner for Rong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dali he was made prefect of Rong and commissioner for Rong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 自安、史之亂，頻詔征發嶺南兵募，隸南陽魯炅軍。

translations.literal: Since the disorders of An and Shi, repeated edicts had summoned and recruited troops from Lingnan, placing them under the army of Lu Kun of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the An Lushan and Shi Siming rebellions, repeated edicts had raised troops in Lingnan and placed them under Lu Kun of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 炅與賊戰於葉縣，大敗，余眾離散。

translations.literal: Kun fought the rebels at Ye County and was utterly defeated; the remaining troops scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Kun fought the rebels at Ye County and suffered a crushing defeat; the survivors dispersed.

sentences.zh: 嶺南溪洞夷獠，乘此相恐為亂，其首領梁崇牽，自號「平南十道大都統」。

translations.literal: The tribal peoples of the streams and caves in Lingnan, taking advantage of this, frightened one another into rebellion; their leader Liang Chongqian styled himself "Grand Commander-in-Chief of the Ten Circuits for Pacifying the South."
translations.idiomatic: The stream-and-cave tribes of Lingnan, exploiting the chaos, stirred one another to revolt; their leader Liang Chongqian styled himself "Grand Commander-in-Chief of the Ten Circuits for Pacifying the South."

sentences.zh: 及其黨覃問等，誘西原賊張侯、夏永攻陷城邑，據容州。

translations.literal: Together with his partisans such as Tan Wen, he incited the Xiyuan rebels Zhang Hou and Xia Yong to attack and seize cities and prefectures, occupying Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He and his followers such as Tan Wen incited the Xiyuan rebels Zhang Hou and Xia Yong to overrun towns and seize Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 前後經略使陳仁琇、李抗、侯令儀、耿慎惑、元結、長孫全緒等，雖容州刺史，皆寄理藤州，或寄梧州。

translations.literal: The successive circuit commissioners Chen Renqiu, Li Kang, Hou Lingyi, Geng Shenhuo, Yuan Jie, and Changsun Quanxu, though titled Prefect of Rong, all administered from Teng Prefecture or from Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Successive commissioners Chen Renqiu, Li Kang, Hou Lingyi, Geng Shenhuo, Yuan Jie, and Changsun Quanxu, though nominally prefects of Rong, all governed from Teng or Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及翃至藤州，言於眾曰：「吾為容州刺史，安得寄理他邑！」

translations.literal: When Hong reached Teng Prefecture, he said to the assembly, "I am the Prefect of Rong—how can I govern from another county!"
translations.idiomatic: When Hong arrived at Teng Prefecture, he told the gathering, "I am prefect of Rong—how can I administer the prefecture from somewhere else!"

sentences.zh: 乃出私財募將健，許奏以好爵，以是人各盡力。

translations.literal: He then spent his private wealth to recruit stalwart soldiers, promising to memorialize the throne for fine ranks and titles, and so each man gave his utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his own money to recruit fighting men, promising to petition the throne for honorable appointments, and each man strove to the limit.

sentences.zh: 不數月，斬賊魁歐陽珪。

translations.literal: Within a few months he beheaded the rebel chieftain Ouyang Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he beheaded the rebel chieftain Ouyang Gui.

sentences.zh: 馳於廣州，見節度使李勉，求兵為援。

translations.literal: He galloped to Guangzhou to see the military commissioner Li Mian and ask for troops as reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: He rode posthaste to Guangzhou to see Military Commissioner Li Mian and request reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 勉曰：「容州陷賊已久，群獠方強，卒難圖也。

translations.literal: Mian said, "Rong has been lost to the rebels for a long time; the tribal forces are still strong and cannot quickly be overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Mian said, "Rong has been in rebel hands for years; the tribal bands are still powerful and cannot be taken at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 若務速攻，只自敗耳，郡不可復也。」

translations.literal: If you insist on a rapid attack, you will only defeat yourself—the prefecture cannot be recovered."
translations.idiomatic: If you press for a hasty assault, you will only ruin yourself—the prefecture cannot be won back."

sentences.zh: 翃請曰：「大夫如未暇出師，但請移牒諸州，揚言出千兵援助，冀藉聲勢，成萬一之功。」

translations.literal: Hong requested, "If the Commissioner is too busy to march, please only dispatch letters to the various prefectures proclaiming that a thousand troops are being sent in aid, hoping to borrow their prestige for a chance of success."
translations.idiomatic: Hong pleaded, "If you cannot march yourself, send dispatches to the prefectures announcing a thousand men in relief—perhaps their reputation alone may win us a slender chance."

sentences.zh: 勉然之。

translations.literal: Mian agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Mian consented.

sentences.zh: 翃乃以手劄告諭義州刺史陳仁璀、藤州刺史李曉庭等，同盟約討賊。

translations.literal: Hong then wrote personal letters notifying Prefect Chen Renrui of Yi Prefecture, Prefect Li Xiaoting of Teng Prefecture, and others, forming an alliance to campaign against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Hong wrote in his own hand to Prefect Chen Renrui of Yi, Prefect Li Xiaoting of Teng, and others, binding them in alliance to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 翃復募三千余人。

translations.literal: Hong recruited more than three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Hong raised another three thousand-odd men.

sentences.zh: 力戰，日數合。

translations.literal: They fought fiercely, clashing several times a day.
translations.idiomatic: They fought hard, meeting in battle several times a day.

sentences.zh: 節度使牒止翃用兵。

translations.literal: The military commissioner sent a dispatch ordering Hong to cease military action.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioner sent orders for Hong to halt operations.

sentences.zh: 翃慮惑將士，匿其牒，奮起士卒，大破賊數萬眾，擒其帥梁崇牽。

translations.literal: Hong, fearing it would unsettle the troops, concealed the dispatch, roused his soldiers, and utterly defeated tens of thousands of rebels, capturing their commander Liang Chongqian.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the order would unsettle his men, Hong hid the dispatch, rallied his troops, and routed tens of thousands of rebels, capturing their leader Liang Chongqian.

sentences.zh: 賊遁數百里外，盡復容州故境。

translations.literal: The rebels fled hundreds of li away, and the former territory of Rong was wholly recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled hundreds of li, and Rong's former borders were fully restored.

sentences.zh: 翃發使以聞，奏置順州，以遏余寇。

translations.literal: Hong sent envoys to report this and memorialized to establish Shun Prefecture to block the remaining bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hong reported the victory and petitioned to establish Shun Prefecture to hem in the remaining raiders.

sentences.zh: 前後大小百余戰，生擒賊帥上獻者七十余人。

translations.literal: In more than a hundred battles large and small, he captured more than seventy rebel chiefs alive and presented them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In over a hundred engagements, great and small, he took more than seventy rebel leaders alive for presentation to the court.

sentences.zh: 累加銀青光祿大夫、兼御史中丞，充招討處置使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and appointed Commissioner for Pacification and Disposition.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted, eventually to Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and made Commissioner for Pacification and Disposition.

sentences.zh: 翃又令其將張利用、李實等分兵討襲西原。

translations.literal: Hong also ordered his generals Zhang Liyong, Li Shi, and others to divide their forces to strike Xiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hong also sent his generals Zhang Liyong, Li Shi, and others in divided columns against Xiyuan.

sentences.zh: 遂收復郁林諸州，部內漸安。

translations.literal: They then recovered the prefectures of Yulin, and peace gradually returned within the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: They recovered the Yulin prefectures, and the circuit gradually settled.

sentences.zh: 後因哥舒晃殺節度使呂崇賁，嶺南復亂。

translations.literal: Later, when Geshu Huang killed the military commissioner Lü Chongben, Lingnan fell into disorder again.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Geshu Huang murdered Military Commissioner Lü Chongben, Lingnan erupted in chaos again.

sentences.zh: 翃遣大將李實悉所管兵赴援廣州。

translations.literal: Hong sent his great general Li Shi with all the troops under his command to aid Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong dispatched his senior general Li Shi with every soldier under his command to relieve Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 西原賊率覃問復招合夷獠曰：「容州兵馬盡赴廣州，郡可圖也。」

translations.literal: The Xiyuan rebel leader Tan Wen again rallied the tribal peoples, saying, "All of Rong's troops and horses have gone to Guangzhou—the prefecture can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Tan Wen, leader of the Xiyuan rebels, again gathered the tribes and said, "Rong's entire force has marched to Guangzhou—the prefecture is ripe for the taking."

sentences.zh: 於是悉眾來襲。

translations.literal: Thereupon they came in full strength to attack.
translations.idiomatic: They then attacked in full strength.

sentences.zh: 翃知其來，伏兵禦之，生擒覃問，其眾大敗。

translations.literal: Hong, knowing they were coming, set an ambush and captured Tan Wen alive; his forces were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Forewarned, Hong laid an ambush, took Tan Wen alive, and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 代宗聞而壯之，遣中使慰勞，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong, hearing of this, admired his feat and sent a palace envoy to comfort and reward him, promoting him to Golden Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong, admiring the feat, sent a palace envoy with rewards and promoted him to Golden Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時西蕃入寇河中，元帥郭子儀統兵備之。

translations.literal: At that time the western Tibetans invaded Hezhong; the commander-in-chief Guo Ziyi led troops to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the western Tibetans raided Hezhong, and Commander-in-Chief Guo Ziyi mobilized to meet them.

sentences.zh: 乃征翃為河中少尹，充節度留後，領子儀之務。

translations.literal: Hong was summoned to be Vice Magistrate of Hezhong and acting military commissioner, taking charge of Ziyi's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was summoned as vice magistrate of Hezhong and acting military commissioner, assuming Ziyi's responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 有悍將淩正者，橫暴擾軍政，約其徒夜噪斬關以逐翃。

translations.literal: There was a fierce general named Ling Zheng who was violent and disturbed military administration; he plotted with his followers to raise a night uproar, cut the gate bars, and drive Hong out.
translations.idiomatic: A brutal officer named Ling Zheng tyrannized the army and plotted with his men to riot by night, break the gate, and expel Hong.

sentences.zh: 有告者，翃縮夜漏數刻，以差其期。

translations.literal: When informants reported this, Hong shortened the night watch by several marks to throw off their timing.
translations.idiomatic: On receiving word, Hong advanced the water-clock several marks to upset their schedule.

sentences.zh: 賊驚而遁，卒誅正，軍城乂安。

translations.literal: The plotters, startled, fled; Ling Zheng was eventually executed, and the garrison and city were restored to order.
translations.idiomatic: The conspirators fled in alarm; Ling Zheng was eventually executed, and the camp and city were secured.

sentences.zh: 歷汾州刺史、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He served successively as Prefect of Fen Prefecture and Magistrate of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Fen and as magistrate of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 屬發涇原兵討李希烈，軍次浐水。

translations.literal: When troops from Jingyuan were mobilized to campaign against Li Xilie, the army halted at Chan River.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingyuan troops were sent against Li Xilie, the army encamped at Chan River.

sentences.zh: 翃備供頓，肉敗糧臭，眾怒以叛。

translations.literal: Hong had prepared supplies, but the meat had spoiled and the grain stank; the troops, enraged, mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had arranged provisions, but the meat had rotted and the grain soured; the soldiers mutinied in fury.

sentences.zh: 翃奔至奉天，加御史大夫，改將作監，從幸山南。

translations.literal: Hong fled to Fengtian, was promoted to Chief Censor, was reassigned as Director of Palace Construction, and accompanied the emperor to Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: Hong fled to Fengtian, was made chief censor, then director of palace construction, and followed the emperor into Shannan.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，改大理卿。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he was made Chief Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the court returned to Chang'an, he was appointed chief justice.

sentences.zh: 出為福州刺史、福建觀察使，入為太子賓客。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Fuzhou and Observation Commissioner of Fujian, then entered court as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Fuzhou and observation commissioner of Fujian, then recalled as mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 貞元十二年，檢校禮部尚書，代董晉為東都留守，判尚書省事、東畿汝防禦使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhenyuan he was made Acting Minister of Rites in place of Dong Jin as Eastern Capital Guardian, directing the Secretariat of the Eastern Capital and Commissioner for the Eastern Capital, Ru, and Fang Defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhenyuan he was made acting minister of rites and replaced Dong Jin as guardian of the eastern capital, directing the secretariat there and serving as commissioner for the eastern capital and the Ru and Fang defense command.

sentences.zh: 凡開置二十余屯，市勁筋良鐵以為兵器，簡練士卒，軍政頗修。

translations.literal: He altogether established more than twenty garrison colonies, purchased strong sinews and fine iron for weapons, drilled the troops, and military administration was considerably improved.
translations.idiomatic: He opened more than twenty garrison colonies, bought stout sinew and good iron for arms, drilled the soldiers, and brought military affairs into good order.

sentences.zh: 無何，吳少誠阻命，翃賦車籍甲，不待完繕，東畿之人賴之。

translations.literal: Before long Wu Shaocheng defied orders; Hong levied carts and registered armor, and though the work was not yet complete, the people of the eastern capital relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Shaocheng rebelled, Hong requisitioned carts and mustered armor; though preparations were unfinished, the eastern capital looked to him for protection.

sentences.zh: 十八年卒，時七十余，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died in the eighteenth year, aged over seventy; he was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year at over seventy and was posthumously given the title minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 郗士美，字和夫，高平金鄉人也。

translations.literal: Chi Shimei, courtesy name Hefu, was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Shimei, whose courtesy name was Hefu, came from Jinxiang in Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 父純，字高卿，為李邕、張九齡等知遇，尤以詞學見推。

translations.literal: His father Chun, courtesy name Gaoqing, won the notice of Li Yong, Zhang Jiuling, and others, and was especially esteemed for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chun, courtesy name Gaoqing, won favor from Li Yong, Zhang Jiuling, and others and was especially admired for letters.

sentences.zh: 與顏真卿、蕭穎士、李華皆相友善。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Yan Zhenqing, Xiao Yingshi, and Li Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with Yan Zhenqing, Xiao Yingshi, and Li Hua.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，繼以書判制策，三中高第，登朝歷拾遺、補闕、員外、郎中、諫議大夫、中書舍人。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, then the written judgment and policy-examination with three top ranks, entered court, and served successively as remonstrance official, supplementer, vice director, director, remonstrance grandee, and Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi, then excelled in the document judgment and policy examinations with three high placings; in court he rose through remonstrance official, supplementer, vice director, director, remonstrance grandee, and secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 處事不回，為元載所忌。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he would not bend, and Yuan Zai resented him.
translations.idiomatic: He would not compromise in office, and Yuan Zai came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩署牙將李琮為兩街功德使。

translations.literal: Yu Chaoen appointed the gate general Li Cong as Commissioner for Merit in the Two Streets.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chaoen appointed the gate general Li Cong commissioner for merit in the Two Streets.

sentences.zh: 琮暴橫，於銀臺門毀辱京兆尹崔昭。

translations.literal: Cong was violent; at the Silver Terrace Gate he insulted Magistrate of the Capital District Cui Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was brutal; at the Silver Terrace Gate he publicly humiliated Capital Magistrate Cui Zhao.

sentences.zh: 純詣元載抗論，以為國恥，請速論奏。

translations.literal: Chun went to Yuan Zai and argued forcefully that this was a national disgrace and asked that it be reported and judged at once.
translations.idiomatic: Chun confronted Yuan Zai, calling the affair a national shame and urging immediate memorialization.

sentences.zh: 載不從，遂以疾辭。

translations.literal: Zai would not comply, and Chun resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zai refused; Chun resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 退歸東洛凡十年，自號「伊川田父。」

translations.literal: He retired to the eastern capital of Luoyang for ten years in all, styling himself "Father of the Fields by the Yi River."
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement at the eastern capital Luoyang for ten years, styling himself "Father of the Fields by the Yi River."

sentences.zh: 清名高節，稱於天下。

translations.literal: His pure name and lofty integrity were praised throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: His unsullied reputation and high integrity were celebrated across the empire.

sentences.zh: 及德宗即位，崔祐甫作相，召拜左庶子、集賢學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Cui Youfu became chief minister and summoned Chun as Left Subdirector and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong acceded, Chief Minister Cui Youfu summoned him as left subdirector and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 到京，以年老乞身，表三上。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital, citing old age he asked to retire and submitted three memorials.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he pleaded age and petitioned three times to retire.

sentences.zh: 除太子詹事致仕，東歸洛陽。

translations.literal: He was made Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household with permission to retire and returned east to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supervisor of the heir apparent's household with permission to retire and went back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 德宗召見，屢加褒嘆，賜以金紫。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong summoned him for audience, repeatedly praised him, and bestowed gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong received him in audience, praised him repeatedly, and granted him gold and the purple robe.

sentences.zh: 公卿大夫皆賦詩祖送於都門，搢紳以為美談。

translations.literal: High ministers and grandees all composed poems to send him off at the capital gate; the gentry regarded it as a fine story.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and grandees composed farewell poems at the city gate; the gentry took it as a celebrated occasion.

sentences.zh: 有文集六十卷行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings in sixty scrolls circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in sixty scrolls circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 士美少好學，善記覽。

translations.literal: Shimei from youth loved learning and was skilled at retaining what he read.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Shimei loved study and had a keen memory.

sentences.zh: 父友顏真卿、蕭潁士輩嘗與之討論經傳，應對如流。

translations.literal: His father's friends Yan Zhenqing, Xiao Yingshi, and others once discussed the classics with him, and his replies flowed freely.
translations.idiomatic: His father's friends Yan Zhenqing, Xiao Yingshi, and others once debated the classics with him; he answered without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 既而相謂曰：「吾曹異日，當交於二郗之間矣。」

translations.literal: Afterward they said to one another, "In days to come we shall be linked with the two Chi families."
translations.idiomatic: They then said to one another, "One day we shall stand between the two houses of Chi."

sentences.zh: 未冠，為陽翟丞。

translations.literal: Before reaching majority he became Assistant Magistrate of Yangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: Before coming of age he became assistant magistrate of Yangzhai.

sentences.zh: 李抱真鎮潞州，辟為從事，雅有參贊之績。

translations.literal: When Li Baozhen governed Luzhou he recruited Shimei as an aide; Shimei distinguished himself in counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Baozhen governed Luzhou he took Shimei on staff; Shimei proved adept in counsel.

sentences.zh: 其後易二帥，皆詔士美佐之。

translations.literal: Afterward two commanders in succession were ordered to have Shimei assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Two successive commanders were each ordered to keep Shimei as his aide.

sentences.zh: 由坊州刺史為黔州刺史、兼御史大夫、持節黔中經略招討觀察鹽鐵等使。

translations.literal: From Prefect of Fang Prefecture he became Prefect of Qian Prefecture, concurrently Chief Censor, and Commissioner for Qianzhong Circuit with authority over pacification, recruitment, observation, and salt and iron.
translations.idiomatic: From prefect of Fang he became prefect of Qian, concurrent chief censor, and commissioner for Qianzhong with authority over pacification, recruitment, observation, and salt and iron.

sentences.zh: 時溪州賊帥向子琪連結夷獠，控據山洞，眾號七八千。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chieftain of Xi Prefecture, Xiang Ziqi, linked up with the tribal peoples, held the mountain caves, and numbered seven or eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Xi Prefecture bandit Xiang Ziqi allied with tribal peoples, held the mountain caves, and mustered seven or eight thousand men.

sentences.zh: 士美設奇略討平之。

translations.literal: Shimei devised a stratagem and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei devised a stratagem and suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 詔書勞慰，加檢校右散騎堂侍，封高平郡公，再遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: An edict commended him; he was made Acting Right Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and enfeoffed Duke of Gaoping, then transferred again to Magistrate of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commended him; he was made acting right regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoping, then transferred again to capital magistrate.

sentences.zh: 每別殿延問，必咨訪大政。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor questioned him in a side hall, he always sought counsel on great affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor received him in a side hall, he was consulted on weighty policy.

sentences.zh: 出為鄂州觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as Observation Commissioner of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as observation commissioner of E.

sentences.zh: 貞元十八年，伊慎有功，特授安黃節度。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhenyuan, because Yi Shen had merit, he was specially made Military Commissioner of An and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Zhenyuan, Yi Shen was specially made military commissioner of An and Huang for his service.

sentences.zh: 二十年，慎來朝，其子宥主留事，朝廷未能去。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Shen came to court; his son You remained in charge, and the court could not remove him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Shen came to court while his son You held the post; the court could not dislodge him.

sentences.zh: 會宥母卒於京師，利主軍權，不時發喪。

translations.literal: When You's mother died in the capital, he coveted control of the army and did not promptly begin mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When You's mother died in the capital, he clung to military authority and delayed the funeral.

sentences.zh: 士美命從事托以他故過其境。

translations.literal: Shimei ordered an aide to pass through the territory on a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei sent a staff member through the territory on a fabricated errand.

sentences.zh: 宥果迎之，告以兇問，先備肩籃，即日遣之。

translations.literal: You indeed received him, was told of the bereavement, and had a carrying basket prepared; he sent him off the same day.
translations.idiomatic: You received him, learned of the death, had a shoulder basket prepared, and dispatched him the same day.

sentences.zh: 元和五年，拜河南尹。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanhe he was made Magistrate of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanhe he was made capital magistrate.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，檢校工部尚書、潞州大都督府長史，充昭義節度。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year he was made Acting Minister of Works, Grand General of Luzhou, and Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the next year he was made acting minister of works, grand general of Luzhou, and military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 前政之豐給浮費，至皆減損，號令嚴肅。

translations.literal: The previous administration had been lavish with floating expenses; upon arrival he reduced them all and his orders were stern.
translations.idiomatic: The prior regime had been wasteful; he cut every extravagance and enforced strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷討王承宗，士美遣兵馬使王獻領勁兵一萬為先鋒。

translations.literal: When the court campaigned against Wang Chengzong, Shimei sent Military Commissioner Wang Xian at the head of ten thousand crack troops as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the court attacked Wang Chengzong, Shimei sent Military Commissioner Wang Xian with ten thousand elite troops as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 獻兇惡恃亂，逗撓不進；

translations.literal: Xian was vicious and relied on disorder; he stalled and would not advance;
translations.idiomatic: Xian was brutal and defiant; he dawdled and refused to advance;

sentences.zh: 遽令召至，數其罪斬之。

translations.literal: Shimei immediately summoned him, recounted his crimes, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei had him summoned at once, listed his crimes, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 下令曰：「敢後出者斬！」

translations.literal: He issued an order: "Whoever leaves camp last will be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed, "Whoever marches out last dies!"

sentences.zh: 士美親鼓之。

translations.literal: Shimei himself beat the drums.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei beat the war drums himself.

sentences.zh: 兵既合，而賊軍大敗，下三營，環柏鄉，屢以捷聞。

translations.literal: Once the armies joined battle the rebel forces were utterly defeated; three camps fell, encircling Baixiang, and repeated victories were reported.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies met the rebels were shattered; three camps were taken, Baixiang was encircled, and victory dispatches followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 上大悅曰：「吾故知士美能辦吾事。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said, "I knew all along that Shimei could handle this for me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and said, "I always knew Shimei could finish this for me."

sentences.zh: 於時四面七、八鎮兵共十余萬，以環鎮、冀，未有首功，多犯法。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of seven or eight circuits on all sides, totaling more than a hundred thousand, encircled Zhen and Ji; there was no first victory, and many broke the law.
translations.idiomatic: At the time seven or eight circuits fielded over a hundred thousand men around Zhen and Ji; no one won the first laurels, and lawlessness was rife.

sentences.zh: 士美兵士勇敢畏法，威聲甚振。

translations.literal: Shimei's soldiers were brave and feared the law; his prestige was greatly enhanced.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei's men were bold yet law-abiding; his authority rang far.

sentences.zh: 承宗大懼，指期有破亡之勢，會詔班師，至今兩河間稱之。

translations.literal: Chengzong was greatly afraid and seemed on the verge of ruin within the appointed time, but an edict ordered withdrawal; to this day he is praised between the two He rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong was terrified and seemed doomed within days, but an edict recalled the armies; to this day he is spoken of with respect in the two He provinces.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以疾征為工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was summoned on account of illness to be Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was recalled, ill, to be minister of works.

sentences.zh: 稍間，拜忠武節度使、檢校刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After a short interval he was made Military Commissioner of Zhongwu and Acting Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made military commissioner of Zhongwu and acting minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 至鎮逾月，寢疾。

translations.literal: A little over a month after reaching his post he fell gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month after taking up the post he fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年九月卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth month of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe (819), aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書左僕射，謚曰景。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and given the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made left vice minister of the secretariat with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 士美善與人交，然諾之際豁如也，當時名稱翕然。

translations.literal: Shimei was skilled at friendship; in keeping promises he was open and forthright, and his reputation at the time was illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei made friends easily and kept his word without reserve; his name shone among contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 李鄘，字建侯，江夏人。

translations.literal: Li Yong, courtesy name Jianhou, was a man of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong, courtesy name Jianhou, was from Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 北海太守邕之侄孫。

translations.literal: He was a grandnephew of Li Yong, Prefect of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: He was a grandnephew of Li Yong, prefect of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 父暄，官至起居舍人。

translations.literal: His father Xuan rose to Attendant of the Bureau of Imperial Seals.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan rose to attendant of the bureau of imperial seals.

sentences.zh: 鄘大歷中舉進士，又以書判高等，授秘書正字。

translations.literal: Yong passed the jinshi in the Dali era and also ranked high in the written judgment examination; he was appointed Corrector of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali period Yong passed the jinshi and ranked high in the document judgment examination; he was made corrector of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 為李懷光所辟，累遷監察御史。

translations.literal: Recruited by Li Huaiguang, he was promoted successively to Surveillance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited by Li Huaiguang, he rose to surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 及懷光據蒲津叛，鄘與母、妻陷賊中。

translations.literal: When Huaiguang held Pu Ford in rebellion, Yong, his mother, and his wife were trapped among the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaiguang rebelled and held Pu Ford, Yong, his mother, and his wife were trapped in rebel territory.

sentences.zh: 恐禍及親，因偽白懷光曰：「兄病在洛，請母往視之。」

translations.literal: Fearing harm to his kin, he falsely told Huaiguang, "My elder brother is ill in Luoyang; I ask that my mother go to see him."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his family, he falsely told Huaiguang, "My brother lies ill in Luoyang—let my mother go to him."

sentences.zh: 懷光許焉，且戒妻子無得從。

translations.literal: Huaiguang consented but warned that wife and children must not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang agreed but forbade wife and children to accompany her.

sentences.zh: 鄘皆遣行。

translations.literal: Yong sent them all away.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent them all off.

sentences.zh: 後懷光知，責之。

translations.literal: Later, when Huaiguang learned of it, he reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaiguang learned of it, he rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「鄘名隸軍籍，不得隨侍老母，奈何不使婦隨姑行也。」

translations.literal: Yong replied, "Yong's name is on the army rolls and I cannot attend my old mother—how can you forbid my wife to go with my mother-in-law?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong answered, "My name is on the rolls and I cannot serve my mother—why should my wife not go with hers?"

sentences.zh: 懷光無以罪之。

translations.literal: Huaiguang had no grounds to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang could find no fault.

sentences.zh: 時與故相高郢同在賊廷，乃密奏賊軍虛實及攻取之勢。

translations.literal: At that time he was together with the former chief minister Gao Ying in the rebel camp and secretly reported the rebels' strength and the prospects for attack and recovery.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was with former chief minister Gao Ying in the rebel camp and secretly reported rebel strength and the chances for recovery.

sentences.zh: 德宗賜手詔以勞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong bestowed a handwritten edict to commend him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong rewarded him with a handwritten edict.

sentences.zh: 後事泄，懷光嚴兵召郢與鄘詰責。

translations.literal: Later the matter leaked out; Huaiguang assembled troops and summoned Ying and Yong to interrogate them.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair leaked, Huaiguang mustered troops and summoned Ying and Yong for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 鄘詞激氣壯，三軍義之。

translations.literal: Yong's words were fierce and his spirit high; the whole army admired his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Yong spoke with fiery defiance; the whole army honored his courage.

sentences.zh: 懷光不敢殺，囚之獄中。

translations.literal: Huaiguang dared not kill them and imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang dared not execute them and threw them in prison.

sentences.zh: 懷光死，馬燧就獄致禮，表為河東從事。

translations.literal: After Huaiguang died, Ma Sui came to the prison with courtesy and memorialized to make Yong an aide in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaiguang's death, Ma Sui visited the prison with full courtesy and petitioned to make Yong an aide in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 尋以言不行，歸養洛中。

translations.literal: Soon, because his advice was not followed, he returned to Luoyang to care for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, when his counsel went unheeded, he retired to Luoyang to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 襄州節度使嗣曹王臯致禮延辟，署從事，奏兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: The Military Commissioner of Xiangzhou, the Prince of Cao, Gao, treated him with respect and recruited him as an aide, memorializing that he also serve as Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou Military Commissioner Prince of Cao Gao honored him, took him on staff, and petitioned for concurrent service as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as vice director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 徐州張建封卒，其子愔為將校所迫，俾領軍務。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou died, his son Yin was compelled by the officers to take command.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou died, his son Yin was forced by the officers to assume command.

sentences.zh: 詔擇臨難不懾者，即其軍以諭之，遂命鄘為徐州宣慰使。

translations.literal: An edict chose one who would not flinch in peril and sent him to that army to instruct them; Yong was appointed Pacification Envoy of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The throne chose a man unafraid in crisis and sent him to that army with instructions; Yong was made pacification envoy of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄘直抵其軍，召將士，傳朝旨，陳禍福，脫監軍使桎梏，令復其位。

translations.literal: Yong went straight to the army, summoned officers and soldiers, conveyed the court's will, explained fortune and ruin, removed the shackles of the army supervisor, and restored him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Yong went straight to camp, assembled the troops, announced the imperial will, weighed gain and loss, removed the army supervisor's bonds, and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 兇黨不敢犯。

translations.literal: The violent faction dared not resist.
translations.idiomatic: The mutinous faction dared not move.

sentences.zh: 及愔上表稱兵馬留後，鄘以為非詔令所加，不宜稱號，立使削去，方受其表。

translations.literal: When Yin submitted a memorial styling himself acting commander of troops and horses, Yong held that this title was not conferred by edict and should not be used; he made him strike it out before accepting the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin memorialized calling himself acting commander of troops and horses, Yong said the title was unauthorized; he made Yin delete it before accepting the document.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 順宗登極，拜御史中丞，遷京兆尹、尚書右丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong took the throne, Yong was made Censor-in-Chief, then Magistrate of the Capital District and Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong acceded, Yong became censor-in-chief, then capital magistrate and right vice minister of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元和初，以京師多盜，復選為京兆尹，擒奸禁暴，威望甚著。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, because the capital had many robbers, he was again chosen as Magistrate of the Capital District; he captured villains and forbade violence, and his prestige was greatly enhanced.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe, with banditry rife in the capital, he was again made capital magistrate; he seized criminals and suppressed violence, and his authority was formidable.

sentences.zh: 尋拜檢校禮部尚書、鳳翔尹、鳳翔隴右節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Acting Minister of Rites, Magistrate of Fengxiang, and Military Commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting minister of rites, magistrate of Fengxiang, and military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 是鎮承前命帥，多用武將，有「神策行營」之號。

translations.literal: That command had long been led by court-appointed generals, mostly military men, and bore the title "Shence Field Headquarters."
translations.idiomatic: That post had long been held by court-appointed generals, mostly soldiers, under the name "Shence Field Headquarters."

sentences.zh: 初受命，必詣軍修謁。

translations.literal: On first receiving appointment one had to visit the army and pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: On appointment one was expected to visit the army and pay homage.

sentences.zh: 鄘既受命，表陳其不可，詔遂去「神策行營」字，但為鳳翔隴右節度。

translations.literal: Once Yong received appointment, he memorialized that this was improper; an edict then removed the words "Shence Field Headquarters," leaving only Military Commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized that this was improper; the throne dropped the words "Shence Field Headquarters," leaving only military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷鎮太原，入為刑部尚書、兼御史大夫、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to command Taiyuan, then entered court as Minister of Justice, concurrently Chief Censor and Transport Commissioner for Salt and Iron of All Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Taiyuan, then recalled as minister of justice, concurrent chief censor and transport commissioner for salt and iron of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，出為揚州大都督府長史、淮南節度使。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year he went out as Grand General of Yangzhou and Military Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year he went out as grand general of Yangzhou and military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 鄘前在兩鎮，皆以剛嚴操下，遽變舊制，人情不安，故未幾即改去。

translations.literal: Yong had earlier governed two commands with stern severity; he suddenly changed old institutions, unsettling popular feeling, and so was soon transferred away.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had ruled two commands with harsh discipline; he abruptly altered old practice, unsettling morale, and was soon moved.

sentences.zh: 至淮南數歲，就加檢校左僕射，政嚴事理，府廩充積。

translations.literal: After several years in Huainan he was made Acting Left Vice Minister; his government was strict and affairs were well ordered, and the granaries were full.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in Huainan he was made acting left vice minister; his rule was strict and orderly, and the storehouses overflowed.

sentences.zh: 及王師征淮夷，鄆寇李師道表裏相援。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against the Huaiyi, the Yan bandit Li Shidao supported them from within and without.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army marched against the Huai rebels, the Yan bandit Li Shidao aided them inside and out.

sentences.zh: 鄘發楚、壽等州二萬餘兵，分壓賊境，日費甚廣，未嘗請於有司。

translations.literal: Yong sent more than twenty thousand troops from Chu, Shou, and other prefectures to press the rebel borders; daily expenses were vast, yet he never asked the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent more than twenty thousand men from Chu, Shou, and other prefectures to pressure the rebel frontier; costs were enormous, yet he never petitioned the central offices.

sentences.zh: 時憲宗以兵興，國用不足，命鹽鐵副使程异乘驛諭江淮諸道，俾助軍用。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xianzong, with war underway and state revenues insufficient, ordered Vice Commissioner for Salt and Iron Cheng Yi to ride posthaste through the Jianghuai circuits to urge military support.
translations.idiomatic: With war draining the treasury, Xianzong sent Vice Commissioner for Salt and Iron Cheng Yi through the Jianghuai circuits to demand military aid.

sentences.zh: 鄘以境內富實，乃大籍府庫，一年所蓄之外，咸貢於朝廷。

translations.literal: Yong, finding his territory rich and secure, made a full inventory of the treasury and presented to the court everything saved beyond one year's stores.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his domain prosperous, Yong inventoried the treasury and sent the court everything beyond a year's reserve.

sentences.zh: 諸道以鄘為倡首，悉索以獻，自此王師無匱乏之憂。

translations.literal: The circuits, taking Yong as their leader, searched out and presented all they could; from then on the imperial army had no fear of shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Other circuits, following Yong's lead, scraped together contributions; thereafter the imperial armies never lacked supplies.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐突承璀監淮南軍，貴寵莫貳。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tutu Chengcui had supervised the Huainan army and was second to none in favor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tutu Chengcui had supervised the Huainan army and stood unrivaled in favor.

sentences.zh: 鄘亦以剛嚴素著，而差相敬憚，未嘗稍失。

translations.literal: Yong was also known for stern severity, yet the two somewhat respected and feared each other and never slipped in propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Yong too was famed for severity; the two respected and feared each other and never breached decorum.

sentences.zh: 承璀歸，遂引以為相。

translations.literal: When Chengcui returned to court he recommended Yong for chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengcui returned to court he recommended Yong for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 十二年，徵拜門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was summoned as vice director of the secretariat and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 鄘出入顯重，素不以公輔自許，年侵勢過，頗安外鎮。

translations.literal: Yong had risen to prominence but never regarded himself as fit for the highest office; as years advanced and his vigor waned, he was quite content in an outer command.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had risen high but never saw himself as chancellor material; as age advanced he preferred life in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 登祖筵，聞樂而泣下，曰：「宰相之任，非吾所長也。」

translations.literal: At the farewell banquet, hearing music he wept and said, "The chancellor's post is not what I am good at."
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell feast, moved by the music, he wept and said, "The chancellorship is not my strength."

sentences.zh: 行頗緩，至京師，又辭疾歸第。

translations.literal: He traveled rather slowly; on reaching the capital he again pleaded illness and returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled slowly; on reaching the capital he again pleaded illness and withdrew to his house.

sentences.zh: 既未朝謁，亦不領政事，竟以疾辭，改授戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He neither attended court audience nor handled government affairs, and eventually resigned on grounds of illness, being reassigned Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He neither attended court nor handled affairs, and finally resigned on grounds of illness, becoming minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 俄換檢校左僕射，兼太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Acting Left Vice Minister, concurrently Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with office at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting left vice minister and mentor of the heir apparent, with duties at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 尋以太子少傅致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he retired as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he retired as junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年八月卒，贈太子太保，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe; he was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Su.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe (820) and was posthumously made grand mentor of the heir apparent with the posthumous title Su.

sentences.zh: 鄘強直無私飾，與楊憑、穆質、許孟容、王仲舒友善，皆任氣自負。

translations.literal: Yong was upright and without artifice; he was friendly with Yang Ping, Mu Zhi, Xu Mengrong, and Wang Zhongshu—all men who trusted their spirit and were proud.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was blunt and unadorned; he was close to Yang Ping, Mu Zhi, Xu Mengrong, and Wang Zhongshu—proud men who trusted their own mettle.

sentences.zh: 然鄘當官嚴重，為吏以峻法立操，所至稱理，而剛決少恩。

translations.literal: Yet in office Yong was grave; as an administrator he established conduct through stern law, and wherever he served he was praised for good order, though his firm decisions showed little mercy.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was grave; he governed by harsh law and was praised for order everywhere he served, though his firmness left little room for mercy.

sentences.zh: 鎮揚州七年，令行禁止。

translations.literal: He governed Yangzhou for seven years; his orders were executed and his prohibitions observed.
translations.idiomatic: For seven years at Yangzhou his commands were obeyed without exception.

sentences.zh: 擒擿生殺，一委軍吏，參佐束手，居人頗陷非法，物議以此少之。

translations.literal: Arrest, exposure, life, and death he wholly entrusted to military clerks; his aides were helpless, and many residents fell afoul of the law; public opinion faulted him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Arrests and executions he left entirely to army clerks; his staff stood idle while many civilians suffered illegal punishment—opinion held this against him.

sentences.zh: 子柱，官至浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: His son Zhu rose to Observation Commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu rose to observation commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 柱子磎，字景望，博學多通，文章秀絕。

translations.literal: Zhu's son Xi, courtesy name Jingwang, was broadly learned and versatile, with writing of surpassing elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu's son Xi, courtesy name Jingwang, was erudite and versatile, his prose exceptionally fine.

sentences.zh: 大中十三年，一舉登進士第。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dazhong he passed the jinshi examination in a single attempt.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Dazhong he passed the jinshi on the first try.

sentences.zh: 歸仁晦鎮大梁，穆仁裕鎮河陽，自監察、殿中相次奏為從事。

translations.literal: When Gui Renhui governed Daliang and Mu Renyu governed Heyang, they successively memorialized to make him an aide, from surveillance censor to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui Renhui governed Daliang and Mu Renyu governed Heyang, they successively petitioned to keep him on staff, from surveillance censor to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書水部員外郎，累遷吏部郎中，兼史館修撰，拜翰林學士、中書舍人。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Director of the Water Bureau in the Secretariat, was promoted successively to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently Compiler of the History Institute, and was made Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as vice director of the water bureau, rose to director of the ministry of personnel and compiler at the History Institute, and was made Hanlin academician and secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 廣明中，分司洛下。

translations.literal: In the Guangming era he held office at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangming period he served at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 遇巢、讓之亂，逃於河橋。

translations.literal: When the disorders of Huang Chao and Shang Rang occurred, he fled to Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: During the disorders of Huang Chao and Shang Rang he fled to Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 光啟中，避亂淮海，有偽襄王詔命，磎皆不從。

translations.literal: In the Guangqi era, fleeing chaos in the Huaihai region, he received false edicts of the bogus Prince of Xiang and refused them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangqi period, fleeing chaos on the Huaihai coast, he rejected every false edict of the bogus Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 王鐸鎮滑臺，杖策詣之。

translations.literal: When Wang Duo governed Huatai, Xi went to him leaning on a staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Duo governed Huatai, Xi came to him staff in hand.

sentences.zh: 鐸表薦於朝。

translations.literal: Duo memorialized recommending him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Duo memorialized recommending him to court.

sentences.zh: 昭宗雅重之，復召入翰林為學士，拜戶部侍郎，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong greatly valued him, recalled him to the Hanlin as academician, made him Vice Minister of Revenue, and promoted him to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong esteemed him, recalled him to the Hanlin, made him vice minister of revenue, then minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 景福二年十月，與韋昭度並命中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Jingfu he was appointed together with Wei Zhaodu as Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Jingfu he was appointed associate chief minister together with Wei Zhaodu.

sentences.zh: 宣制日，水部郎中、知制誥劉崇魯掠其麻哭之，奏云：「李磎奸邪，挾附權幸，以忝學士，不合為相。」

translations.literal: On the day the appointment was proclaimed, Director of the Water Bureau and Drafter of Edicts Liu Chonglu snatched his appointment document and wept over it, memorializing, "Li Xi is treacherous and wicked, clinging to the powerful and favored; he disgraces the post of academician and is unfit to be chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: On proclamation day Liu Chonglu, director of the water bureau and drafter of edicts, seized Xi's appointment scroll and wept, memorializing, "Li Xi is treacherous, clinging to the powerful; he disgraces the Hanlin and is unfit for the chancellorship."

sentences.zh: 時宰臣崔昭緯與昭度及磎素不相協，密遣崇魯沮之也，乃左授太子少師。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Minister Cui Zhaowei was at odds with Zhaodu and Xi and secretly sent Chonglu to obstruct the appointment; Xi was therefore demoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Cui Zhaowei, hostile to Zhaodu and Xi, secretly sent Chonglu to block the appointment; Xi was demoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 磎因上十章及《納諫論》三篇自雪，且數崇魯之惡。

translations.literal: Xi then submitted ten memorials and three essays, "On Receiving Remonstrance," to clear himself and enumerated Chonglu's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Xi submitted ten memorials and three essays On Receiving Remonstrance to clear himself and denounced Chonglu.

sentences.zh: 議者重其才而鄙其訟。

translations.literal: Commentators valued his talent but despised his litigiousness.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion respected his talent but scorned his quarrelsomeness.

sentences.zh: 昭宗素愛其才，而急於大用。

translations.literal: Zhaozong had always loved his talent and was eager to employ him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong had long prized his talent and wished to promote him.

sentences.zh: 至乾寧初，又上第十一表，乃復命為相。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Qianning he submitted an eleventh memorial and was again appointed chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianning, after an eleventh memorial, he was again made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 數月，與昭度同為王行瑜等所殺。

translations.literal: Within a few months he was killed together with Zhaodu by Wang Xingyu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he and Zhaodu were killed by Wang Xingyu and his faction.

sentences.zh: 磎自在臺省，聚書至多，手不釋卷，時人號曰「李書樓」。

translations.literal: From the time Xi was in the Censorate and Secretariat he amassed many books and never put a scroll down; contemporaries called him "Li the Book Tower."
translations.idiomatic: From his years in the censorate and secretariat Xi amassed books and never laid a scroll aside; men called him "Li the Book Tower."

sentences.zh: 所撰文章及註解書傳之闕疑，僅百余卷，經亂悉亡。

translations.literal: The writings he composed and his annotations resolving doubts in books and transmissions amounted to barely more than a hundred scrolls; all were lost in the disorders.
translations.idiomatic: His writings and commentaries filling lacunae in the classics totaled barely a hundred scrolls; all were lost in the chaos.

sentences.zh: 王行瑜死，德音昭雪，贈司徒，謚曰文。

translations.literal: After Wang Xingyu died, an amnesty edict cleared his name; he was posthumously made Grand Mentor and given the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Xingyu's death an amnesty restored his name; he was posthumously made grand mentor with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子沇，字東濟，有俊才。

translations.literal: His son Yan, courtesy name Dongji, had outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan, courtesy name Dongji, had remarkable talent.

sentences.zh: 與父同日遇害，詔贈禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was killed on the same day as his father; an edict posthumously awarded him Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed the same day as his father; an edict posthumously made him vice director of the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 辛秘，隴西人。

translations.literal: Xin Mi was a man of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Mi was from Longxi.

sentences.zh: 少嗜學。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved study.

sentences.zh: 貞元年中，累登《五經》、《開元禮》科，選授華原尉，判入高等，調補長安尉。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era he repeatedly passed the examinations in the Five Classics and the Kaiyuan Rites; he was selected and appointed Defender of Huayuan, ranked high in judgment, and transferred to supplement Defender of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era he repeatedly passed the Five Classics and Kaiyuan Rites examinations, was appointed defender of Huayuan, ranked high in evaluation, and was transferred to defender of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高郢為太常卿，嘉其禮學，奏授太常博士。

translations.literal: When Gao Ying was Minister of Ceremonies he admired Mi's ritual learning and memorialized to appoint him Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Ying was minister of ceremonies he admired Mi's ritual scholarship and petitioned to make him erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 遷祠部、兵部員外郎，仍兼博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Supplications and Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, still concurrently serving as erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice director of the bureaus of supplications and of military affairs while retaining his erudite post.

sentences.zh: 山陵及郊丘二禮儀使，皆署為判官。

translations.literal: The commissioners for the rites of the imperial tomb and suburban sacrifices both appointed him as magistrate's aide.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioners for the imperial tomb and suburban sacrifice rites both named him aide.

sentences.zh: 當時推其達禮。

translations.literal: At the time he was acclaimed for mastery of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised his mastery of ritual.

sentences.zh: 元和初，拜湖州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was made Prefect of Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he was made prefect of Hu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，屬李锜命，將收支郡，遂令大將監守五郡。

translations.literal: Before long, on Li Qi taking command, intending to absorb the subordinate prefectures, he ordered a great general to garrison and oversee five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Li Qi took command, intending to absorb the subordinate prefectures, he stationed a senior general to oversee five of them.

sentences.zh: 蘇常杭睦四州刺史，或以戰敗，或被拘執。

translations.literal: The prefects of Su, Chang, Hang, and Mu were either defeated in battle or taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: The prefects of Su, Chang, Hang, and Mu were either defeated or captured.

sentences.zh: 賊黨以秘儒者，甚易之。

translations.literal: The rebel faction, seeing that Mi was a scholar, greatly underestimated him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, seeing Mi was a scholar, took him lightly.

sentences.zh: 秘密遣衙門將丘知二勒兵數百人，候賊將動，逆戰大破之。

translations.literal: Mi secretly sent the gate general Qiu Zhier with several hundred troops; when the rebel general moved, they met him in battle and utterly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Mi secretly sent Gate General Qiu Zhier with several hundred men; when the rebel column moved, they intercepted and routed it.

sentences.zh: 知二中流矢墜馬，起而復戰，斬其將，焚其營，一州遂安。

translations.literal: Zhier was struck by a flying arrow and fell from his horse, but rose and fought again, beheading the enemy general, burning their camp, and the prefecture was secured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhier took an arrow, fell from his horse, rose and fought on, beheaded the enemy commander, burned the camp, and the prefecture was saved.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以功賜金紫，由是僉以秘材堪將帥。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, for his merit he was awarded gold and purple; from then on all agreed Mi had the talent of a general.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed he was awarded gold and purple; thereafter all agreed Mi had the makings of a commander.

sentences.zh: 及太原節度範希朝領全師出討王承宗，征秘為河東行軍司馬，委以留務。

translations.literal: When Fan Xichao of Taiyuan led the full army to campaign against Wang Chengzong, Mi was summoned as Military Secretary of the Hedong Field Army and entrusted with affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Xichao of Taiyuan marched against Wang Chengzong with his full force, Mi was summoned as military secretary of the Hedong field army and left in charge of the rear.

sentences.zh: 尋召拜左司郎中，出為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Left Director of the Department of State Affairs and went out as Prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as left director of the department of state affairs, then sent out as prefect of Ru.

sentences.zh: 九年，征拜諫議大夫，改常州刺史，選為河南尹。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned as Remonstrance Grandee, changed to Prefect of Chang Prefecture, and chosen as Magistrate of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made remonstrance grandee, then prefect of Chang, then chosen as capital magistrate.

sentences.zh: 蒞職修政，有可稱者。

translations.literal: In office he improved government, and there were matters worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: In office he improved administration and earned praise.

sentences.zh: 十二年，拜檢校工部尚書，代郗士美為潞州大都督府長史、御史大夫，充昭義軍節度、澤潞磁洺邢等州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was made Acting Minister of Works, replacing Chi Shimei as Grand General of Luzhou and Chief Censor, Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi Army, and Observation Commissioner of Ze, Lu, Ci, Ming, and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made acting minister of works, replacing Chi Shimei as grand general of Luzhou and chief censor, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, and observation commissioner of Ze, Lu, Ci, Ming, and Xing.

sentences.zh: 是時以再討王承宗，澤潞壓境，雕費尤甚。

translations.literal: At that time, because Wang Chengzong was being attacked again, Ze and Lu bordered the enemy and waste was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Chengzong under attack again, Ze and Lu lay on the frontier and had suffered especially heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 朝議以兵革之後，思能完復者，遂以命秘。

translations.literal: Court opinion, thinking that after war what was needed was someone who could fully restore order, entrusted this to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: The court, seeking someone who could rebuild after war, entrusted the post to Mi.

sentences.zh: 凡四歲，府庫積錢七十萬貫，餱糧器械稱是。

translations.literal: In four years the treasury accumulated seven hundred thousand strings of cash, and provisions, grain, and equipment were adequate.
translations.idiomatic: In four years the treasury amassed seven hundred thousand strings of cash; grain, fodder, and arms were sufficient.

sentences.zh: 及歸，道病，先自為墓誌。

translations.literal: On returning, he fell ill on the road and beforehand composed his own epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey home he fell ill and beforehand wrote his own epitaph.

sentences.zh: 將歿，又為書一通，命緘致幾上。

translations.literal: As death approached he also wrote a single letter and ordered it sealed and placed on the table.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he also wrote one letter and ordered it sealed on his desk.

sentences.zh: 其家發之，皆送終遵儉之旨。

translations.literal: When his family opened it, it contained only instructions for a frugal funeral.
translations.idiomatic: His family opened it and found only instructions for a spare funeral.

sentences.zh: 久歷重任，無豐財厚產，為時所稱。

translations.literal: Though he had long held weighty posts, he left no great wealth or rich estates, and was praised by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had long held high office, he left no great fortune; contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年十二月卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: He died in the twelfth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe (820), aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈左僕射，謚曰昭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Left Vice Minister and given the posthumous title Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made left vice minister with the posthumous title Zhao.

sentences.zh: 馬摠，字會元，扶風人。

translations.literal: Ma Zong, courtesy name Huiyuan, was a man of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zong, courtesy name Huiyuan, was from Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧好學。

translations.literal: From youth he was orphaned and poor but loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor from youth, he loved learning.

sentences.zh: 性剛直，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and firm; he did not associate lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and would not make friends lightly.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，姚南仲鎮滑臺，辟為從事。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era, when Yao Nanzhong governed Huatai, he recruited Zong as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era, when Yao Nanzhong governed Huatai, he took Zong on staff.

sentences.zh: 南仲與監軍使不葉，監軍誣奏南仲不法。

translations.literal: Nanzhong and the army supervisor were at odds; the supervisor falsely reported that Nanzhong had broken the law.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong quarreled with the army supervisor, who falsely reported his misconduct.

sentences.zh: 及罷免，摠坐貶泉州別駕，監軍入掌樞密。

translations.literal: When Nanzhong was dismissed, Zong was implicated and demoted to Vice Prefect of Quanzhou; the supervisor entered court to hold the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanzhong was removed, Zong was demoted to vice prefect of Quanzhou; the supervisor entered court to dominate the privy council.

sentences.zh: 福建觀察使柳冕希旨欲殺摠，從事穆贊鞫摠，贊稱無罪，摠方免死。

translations.literal: The Observation Commissioner of Fujian, Liu Mian, eager to please, wished to kill Zong; the aide Mu Zan tried Zong and declared him innocent, and only then was Zong spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian Observation Commissioner Liu Mian, eager to please, sought to kill Zong; staff member Mu Zan tried him and found no guilt, sparing his life.

sentences.zh: 後量移恩王傅。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred by quota to Tutor of the Prince of En.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred by quota to tutor of the Prince of En.

sentences.zh: 元和初，遷虔州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was transferred to Prefect of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he was made prefect of Qian.

sentences.zh: 四年，兼御史中丞，充嶺南都護、本管經略使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was concurrently Chief Censor and Protector-General of Lingnan and Commissioner for that Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made concurrent chief censor, protector-general of Lingnan, and commissioner for that circuit.

sentences.zh: 摠敦儒學，長於政術。

translations.literal: Zong honored Confucian learning and excelled in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zong honored Confucian learning and excelled in administration.

sentences.zh: 在南海累年，清廉不撓，夷獠便之。

translations.literal: For many years in the South Sea he was incorruptible and unyielding, and the tribal peoples found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: For years on the southern sea he was incorruptible and unbending; the tribes found him just.

sentences.zh: 於漢所立銅柱之處，以銅一千五百斤特鑄二柱，刻書唐德，以繼伏波之跡。

translations.literal: At the place where the Han had erected bronze pillars, he specially cast two pillars with fifteen hundred jin of bronze, inscribing Tang virtue to continue the traces of Ma Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Han had set bronze pillars, he cast two new ones from fifteen hundred jin of bronze, inscribing Tang virtue to follow Ma Yuan's precedent.

sentences.zh: 以綏蠻功，就加金紫。

translations.literal: For pacifying the barbarians he was made Golden Radiance Grand Master on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying the tribes he was immediately awarded golden radiance grand master.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉桂州刺史、桂管經略觀察使，入為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Prefect of Gui Prefecture and Commissioner for Observation of Gui Circuit, then entered court as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became prefect of Gui and observation commissioner of Gui Circuit, then entered court as vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 裴度宣慰淮西，奏為制置副使。

translations.literal: When Pei Du went to pacify Huaixi he memorialized to make Zong Vice Commissioner for Disposition.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du pacified Huaixi he petitioned to make Zong vice commissioner for disposition.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟誅，度留摠蔡州，知彰義軍留後。

translations.literal: After Wu Yuanji was executed, Du left Zong at Caizhou as acting commander of the Zhangyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Yuanji was executed, Du left Zong at Caizhou as acting commander of the Zhangyi army.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校工部尚書、蔡州刺史、兼御史大夫，充淮西節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Acting Minister of Works, Prefect of Cai Prefecture, concurrently Chief Censor, and Military Commissioner of Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting minister of works, prefect of Cai, concurrent chief censor, and military commissioner of Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 摠以申、光、蔡等州久陷賊寇，人不知法，威刑勸導，咸令率化。

translations.literal: Zong, because Shen, Guang, and Cai and other prefectures had long been under rebel bandits and the people knew no law, used stern punishment and guidance, and all were led to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shen, Guang, Cai, and other prefectures had long been under rebels and knew no law, Zong governed by stern example until all were reformed.

sentences.zh: 奏改彰義軍曰淮西，賊之偽跡，一皆削蕩。

translations.literal: He memorialized to change the Zhangyi Army to Huaixi, and every trace of the rebels was wholly swept away.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to rename the Zhangyi army Huaixi and erased every vestige of the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 十三年，轉許州刺史、忠武軍節度、陳許溵等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Prefect of Xu Prefecture, Military Commissioner of Zhongwu Army, and Commissioner for Observation and Disposition of Chen, Xu, and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became prefect of Xu, military commissioner of Zhongwu, and commissioner for observation and disposition of Chen, Xu, and Wen.

sentences.zh: 明年，改華州刺史、潼關防禦、鎮國軍等使。

translations.literal: The following year he was changed to Prefect of Hua Prefecture, Defender of Tong Pass, and Commissioner of Zhenguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became prefect of Hua, defender of Tong Pass, and commissioner of Zhenguo army.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷檢校刑部尚書、鄆州刺史、天平軍節度、鄆曹濮等州觀察等使，就加檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Acting Minister of Justice, Prefect of Yan Prefecture, Military Commissioner of Tianping Army, and Observation Commissioner of Yan, Cao, and Pu, and was made Acting Left Vice Minister on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became acting minister of justice, prefect of Yan, military commissioner of Tianping, observation commissioner of Yan, Cao, and Pu, and was immediately made acting left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He entered court as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年卒，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Changqing and was posthumously made Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Changqing (823) and was posthumously made right vice minister.

sentences.zh: 摠理道素優，軍政多暇，公務之余，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Zong's governance had always been excellent; in military administration he had much leisure, and beyond public duties he never put a book down.
translations.idiomatic: Zong had always governed well; with military affairs in order he had leisure, and outside office never laid a book aside.

sentences.zh: 所著《奏議集》、《年歷》、《通歷》、《子鈔》等書百余卷，行於世。

translations.literal: His works "Collected Memorials," "Chronological Calendar," "Comprehensive Calendar," and "Extracts of the Masters," more than a hundred scrolls in all, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Collected Memorials, Chronological Calendar, Comprehensive Calendar, and Extracts of the Masters—more than a hundred scrolls—circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 韋弘景，京兆人，後周逍遙公夐之後。

translations.literal: Wei Hongjing was a man of the Capital District and a descendant of Wei Jiong, Duke of Xiaoyao of the Later Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hongjing was from the capital district and descended from Wei Jiong, Duke of Xiaoyao of the Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 祖嗣立，終宣州司戶。

translations.literal: His grandfather Silizhi ended as Registrar of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Silizhi ended as registrar of Xu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父堯，終洋州興道令。

translations.literal: His father Yao ended as Magistrate of Xingdao in Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yao ended as magistrate of Xingdao in Yang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弘景貞元中始舉進士，為汴州、浙東從事。

translations.literal: Hongjing first passed the jinshi in the Zhenyuan era and served as an aide in Bian Prefecture and Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing first passed the jinshi in the Zhenyuan era and served on staff in Bian and Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 元和三年，拜左拾遺，充集賢殿學士，轉左補闕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhe he was made Left Remonstrance Official, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and transferred to Left Supplementer.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhe he was made left remonstrance official and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then left supplementer.

sentences.zh: 尋召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to the Hanlin as academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned to the Hanlin as academician.

sentences.zh: 普潤鎮使蘇光榮為涇原節度使，弘景草麻，漏敘光榮之功，罷學士，改司門員外郎，轉吏部員外、左司郎中，改吏部度支郎中。

translations.literal: When Su Guangrong, commander of Puerun, became Military Commissioner of Jingyuan, Hongjing drafted the appointment edict but omitted Guangrong's achievements; he was dismissed from the Hanlin, made Vice Director of the Gate Office, transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Left Director of the Department of State Affairs, and changed to Director of Revenue in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Guangrong of Puerun became military commissioner of Jingyuan, Hongjing drafted the edict but omitted his achievements; he was dismissed from the Hanlin, made vice director of the gate office, then vice director of personnel and left director of state affairs, then director of revenue in personnel.

sentences.zh: 張仲方貶李吉甫謚，上怒，貶仲方。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhongfang criticized the posthumous title of Li Jifu, the emperor was angry and demoted Zhongfang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhongfang attacked Li Jifu's posthumous title, the emperor was angry and demoted him.

sentences.zh: 弘景坐與仲方善，出為綿州刺史。

translations.literal: Hongjing, because he was friendly with Zhongfang, was sent out as Prefect of Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hongjing was close to Zhongfang, he was sent out as prefect of Mian.

sentences.zh: 宰相李夷簡出鎮淮南，奏為副使，賜以金紫。

translations.literal: When Chief Minister Li Yijian went out to govern Huainan he memorialized to make Hongjing his deputy and bestowed gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Minister Li Yijian went to Huainan he petitioned for Hongjing as deputy and granted him gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 入為京兆少尹，遷給事中。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Magistrate of the Capital District and was promoted to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as vice capital magistrate, then drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 劉士涇以駙馬交通邪幸，穆宗用為太僕卿。

translations.literal: Liu Shijing, by virtue of being an imperial son-in-law, curried favor with wicked favorites; Muzong employed him as Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shijing, an imperial son-in-law, trafficked with corrupt favorites; Muzong appointed him minister of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 弘景與給事薛存慶封還詔書，諭士涇曰：「伏以司僕正卿，位居九列。

translations.literal: Hongjing and Drafting Attendant Xue Cunqing returned the edict sealed shut and addressed Shijing, "We submit that the Minister of the Imperial Stud, Director of the First Rank among the Nine Ministers,
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing and Drafting Attendant Xue Cunqing sealed the edict shut and addressed Shijing: "We submit that the minister of the imperial stud, a minister of the first rank among the nine ministries,

sentences.zh: 在周之命，伯冏其人，所以惟月膺名，象河稱重。

translations.literal: In the appointments of Zhou, Bo Jiong was such a man; hence the moon receives the name, and the river symbolizes weight.
translations.idiomatic: in Zhou's appointments Bo Jiong held this office; hence the moon receives its title and the river its weight.

sentences.zh: 漢朝亦以石慶之謹願，陳萬年之行潔，皆踐斯職，謂之大僚。

translations.literal: The Han dynasty too appointed the careful and sincere Shi Qing and the upright in conduct Chen Wannian—all trod this office and were called great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Han too appointed the scrupulous Shi Qing and the upright Chen Wannian—each held this post and was called a great minister.

sentences.zh: 今士涇戚里常人，班敘散秩，以父任將帥，家富貲財，聲名不在於士林，行義無聞於朝野，忽長卿寺，有瀆官常。

translations.literal: Now Shijing is an ordinary man by imperial marriage, ranked in the scattered grades; through his father's appointment as a general his family is rich in wealth; his reputation is not among the literati, and his conduct is unheard of at court—suddenly to head the Stud Ministry violates regular office.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing is a common in-law, ranked among the scattered grades; his father was a general and the family is wealthy; he is unknown among scholars and unheard of at court—suddenly to head the stud ministry violates proper appointment.

sentences.zh: 以親則人物未賢，以勳則寵待常厚，今叨顯任，誠謂謬官。
