translations.literal: As kin he is not a worthy man; as merit his favor has always been thick—now to receive so exalted a post is truly to call it a mistaken appointment.
translations.idiomatic: By kinship he is no worthy man; by merit his favor has always been lavish—to give him so lofty a post is plainly a mistaken appointment.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『惟名與器，不可假人。』

translations.literal: The Transmission says, 'Titles and regalia must not be lent to others.'
translations.idiomatic: The Transmission says, 'Titles and regalia must not be lent to others.'

sentences.zh: 蓋士涇之謂。

translations.literal: This surely refers to Shijing.
translations.idiomatic: This surely refers to Shijing.

sentences.zh: 臣等職司違失，實在守官。

translations.literal: We, in the dereliction of our office, are truly at fault for guarding our posts.
translations.idiomatic: We have failed in duty by guarding our posts.

sentences.zh: 其劉士涇新除太僕卿敕，未敢行下。」

translations.literal: The new appointment of Liu Shijing as Minister of the Imperial Stud—we dare not promulgate it."
translations.idiomatic: The new appointment of Liu Shijing as minister of the imperial stud—we dare not promulgate it."

sentences.zh: 穆宗遣宰臣宣諭，弘景等固執如前。

translations.literal: Muzong sent chief ministers to explain; Hongjing and the others stood firm as before.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong sent chief ministers to explain; Hongjing and the others held firm.

sentences.zh: 宰臣不得已，改衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: The chief ministers had no choice and changed the appointment to Vice Minister of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers had no choice and changed the post to vice minister of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 穆宗復遣諭弘景曰：「士涇父昌有邊功，士涇為少列十餘年，又尚雲安公主，宜有加恩。

translations.literal: Muzong again sent word to Hongjing, "Shijing's father Chang had merit on the frontier; Shijing has been in the junior ranks for more than ten years and has married Princess Yun'an—he should receive added favor.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong again sent word to Hongjing: "Shijing's father Chang had frontier merit; Shijing has held junior rank for more than ten years and married Princess Yun'an—he deserves added favor.

sentences.zh: 朕思賞勞睦親之意，竟行前命。」

translations.literal: I think of rewarding merit and cherishing kin—carry out the original appointment."
translations.idiomatic: I mean to reward service and cherish kin—carry out the original appointment."

sentences.zh: 穆宗怒，乃令弘景使安南、邕、容宣慰，時認翕然推重。

translations.literal: Muzong was angry and therefore sent Hongjing as envoy to pacify Annan, Yong, and Rong; at the time opinion unanimously esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Angry, Muzong sent Hongjing as envoy to pacify Annan, Yong, and Rong; opinion unanimously respected him.

sentences.zh: 時蕭俛以清直在位，弘景議論，常所輔助。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Mian was in office for his purity and uprightness; Hongjing's deliberations were often assisted by him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Mian served for his purity; Hongjing often found support in his counsel.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部侍郎，轉吏部侍郎，銓綜平允，權邪憚其嚴勁，不敢干以非道。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice, then Vice Minister of Personnel; in selection and evaluation he was fair, and the powerful and wicked feared his stern force and dared not approach him by improper means.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of justice, then vice minister of personnel; his selections were evenhanded, and the powerful feared his sternness and dared not approach him improperly.

sentences.zh: 掌選二歲，改陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: After two years in charge of selection he was made Observation Commissioner of Shaan and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: After two years managing selection he was made observation commissioner of Shaan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，征拜尚書左丞，駁吏部授官不當者六十人。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was summoned as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and rejected sixty improper appointments made by the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was summoned as left vice director and rejected sixty improper personnel appointments.

sentences.zh: 弘景素以鯁亮稱，及居綱轄之地，郎吏望風修整。

translations.literal: Hongjing had always been known for blunt integrity; once he held the reins of office, clerks reformed themselves at the sight of him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing had always been famed for blunt integrity; once he held authority, clerks straightened themselves at his glance.

sentences.zh: 會吏部員外郎楊虞卿以公事為下吏所訕，獄未能辨，詔下弘景與憲司就尚書省詳讞。

translations.literal: When Vice Director of Personnel Yang Yuqing was reviled by a subordinate clerk over public business and the case could not be resolved, an edict ordered Hongjing and the Censorate to conduct a detailed inquiry at the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Director Yang Yuqing was slandered by a clerk in a public matter and the case stalled, an edict ordered Hongjing and the censorate to investigate at the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 虞卿多朋遊，人多向附之。

translations.literal: Yuqing had many friends; many people inclined to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing had many friends; many sided with him.

sentences.zh: 弘景素所不悅，時已請告在第，及準詔就召，以公服來謁。

translations.literal: Hongjing had never liked him; he had already requested leave and was at home when, in accordance with the edict, he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing disliked him; already on leave at home, he came when summoned under the edict.

sentences.zh: 弘景謂之曰：「有敕推公。」

translations.literal: Hongjing said to him, "There is an edict to investigate you."
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing told him, "There is an edict to investigate you."

sentences.zh: 虞卿失容自退。

translations.literal: Yuqing, losing composure, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing, stricken, withdrew.

sentences.zh: 轉禮部尚書，充東都留守，判東都尚書省事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites and made Guardian of the Eastern Capital, directing the Secretariat of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of rites, guardian of the eastern capital, directing the eastern secretariat.

sentences.zh: 繕完宮室，至今賴之。

translations.literal: He repaired the palaces; to this day they rely on his work.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the palatial buildings; the eastern capital still relies on his work.

sentences.zh: 太和五年五月卒，年六十六，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth month of the fifth year of Taihe, aged sixty-six, and was posthumously made Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of the fifth year of Taihe (831), aged sixty-six, and was posthumously made left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 弘景歷官行事，始終以直道自立，議論操持，無所阿附，當時風教，尤為倚賴。

translations.literal: In his conduct through all offices Hongjing always upheld the straight path; in deliberation and self-restraint he never curried favor, and the customs of the time especially relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: In every post Hongjing stood on the straight path; in counsel he never flattered, and the age especially relied on him.

sentences.zh: 自長慶已來，目為名卿。

translations.literal: From the Changqing era onward he was regarded as a celebrated minister.
translations.idiomatic: From the Changqing era onward he was counted among celebrated ministers.

sentences.zh: 王彥威，太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Yanwei was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanwei was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 世儒家，少孤貧苦學，尤通《三禮》。

translations.literal: His family for generations were Confucian scholars; orphaned and poor from youth, he studied bitterly and was especially versed in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His family were scholars for generations; orphaned and poor, he studied hard and was especially versed in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 無由自達，元和中遊京師，求為太常散吏。

translations.literal: With no means to advance himself, in the Yuanhe era he traveled to the capital seeking to be a minor clerk of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to advance, in the Yuanhe era he went to the capital seeking a minor post at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 卿知其書生，補充檢討官。

translations.literal: The minister, knowing he was a scholar, appointed him to the post of collator.
translations.idiomatic: The minister, seeing he was a scholar, appointed him collator.

sentences.zh: 彥威於禮閣掇拾自隋已來朝廷沿革、吉兇五禮，以類區分，成三十卷獻之，號曰《元和新禮》，由是知名，特授太常博士。

translations.literal: Yanwei gathered from the ritual archives, from Sui onward, the court's reforms and the five rites of auspice and inauspice, classified them by category, completed thirty scrolls, and presented them, titled "New Rites of the Yuanhe"; thereby he became known and was specially appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei gathered from the ritual archives, from Sui onward, court reforms and the five rites of auspice and inauspice, arranged them in thirty scrolls as New Rites of the Yuanhe, and was thereby famed and specially made erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 憲宗晏駕，未定謚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong died, the posthumous title was undecided.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong died, his temple title was undecided.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使李夷簡以憲宗功高列聖，宜特稱祖，穆宗下禮官議。

translations.literal: The Military Commissioner of Huainan, Li Yijian, held that because Xianzong's merit surpassed the sage emperors, he should specially be called Ancestor; Muzong ordered the ritual officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan Military Commissioner Li Yijian argued that Xianzong's merit surpassed the sage emperors and he should be specially styled Ancestor; Muzong ordered the ritual officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 彥威奏曰：「據禮經，三代之制，始封之君，謂之太祖。

translations.literal: Yanwei memorialized, "According to the ritual classics, in the institutions of the Three Dynasties, the first enfeoffed ruler is called Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei memorialized: "According to the ritual classics, in the Three Dynasties the first enfeoffed ruler is called Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太祖之外，又祖有功而宗有德，故夏後氏祖顓頊而宗禹，殷人祖契而宗湯，周人郊祀后稷，祖文王而宗武王。

translations.literal: Beyond the Grand Ancestor, one further honors those with merit as ancestors and those with virtue as exemplars; thus the Xia honored Zhuanxu and took Yu as exemplar, the Yin honored Qi and took Tang as exemplar, and the Zhou in suburban sacrifice honored Houji, taking King Wen as ancestor and King Wu as exemplar.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Grand Ancestor, those with merit become ancestors and those with virtue exemplars: Xia honored Zhuanxu and took Yu as exemplar; Yin honored Qi and Tang as exemplar; Zhou in suburban sacrifice honored Houji, taking King Wen as ancestor and King Wu as exemplar.

sentences.zh: 自東漢魏晉，漸違經意，沿革不一。

translations.literal: From Eastern Han and Wei-Jin onward they gradually departed from the meaning of the classics, with reforms not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: From Eastern Han and Wei-Jin they gradually departed from the classics, with inconsistent reforms.

sentences.zh: 子孫以推美為先，自始祖已下並有建祖之制。

translations.literal: Descendants, putting praise first, from the Founding Ancestor downward all had the institution of establishing ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants, eager for praise, from the founding ancestor downward all established ancestor-titles.

sentences.zh: 蓋非典訓，不可法也。

translations.literal: This is not canonical instruction and cannot be taken as model.
translations.idiomatic: This is not canonical and cannot be imitated.

sentences.zh: 國朝祖宗制度，本於《周禮》，以景皇帝為太祖，又祖神堯而宗太宗。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's ancestral institutions, based on the 'Rites of Zhou,' take Emperor Jing as Grand Ancestor, and further honor Shen Yao as ancestor and Taizong as exemplar.
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestral system, based on the Rites of Zhou, takes Emperor Jing as Grand Ancestor, honors Shen Yao as ancestor and Taizong as exemplar.

sentences.zh: 自高宗已降，但稱宗。

translations.literal: From Gaozong downward they are only called Exemplars.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozong downward they are styled only Exemplar.

sentences.zh: 謂之尊名，可為成法。

translations.literal: This is called honoring the name and may serve as established law.
translations.idiomatic: This is called honoring the title and may stand as settled law.

sentences.zh: 不然，則太宗造有區夏，理致升平；

translations.literal: Otherwise, Taizong created the realm and brought order and peace;
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Taizong founded the realm and brought peace;

sentences.zh: 玄宗掃清內難，翊戴聖父；

translations.literal: Xuanzong swept away internal troubles and supported the sage father;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong quelled internal strife and upheld the sage father;

sentences.zh: 肅宗龍飛靈武，收復兩都，此者應天順人，撥亂返正，至於廟號，亦但稱宗。

translations.literal: Suzong rose at Lingwu and recovered the two capitals—these answered Heaven and followed the people, restored order from chaos, yet for temple titles they too are only called Exemplar.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong rose at Lingwu and recovered the two capitals—each answered Heaven, turned chaos to order—yet their temple titles too are only Exemplar.

sentences.zh: 謹按經義，祖者始也，宗者尊也，故《傳》曰：『始封必為祖。』

translations.literal: Respectfully according to the meaning of the classics, ancestor means beginning and exemplar means honor; thus the Transmission says, 'The first enfeoffment must be made ancestor.'
translations.idiomatic: By the classics, ancestor means beginning and exemplar means honor; the Transmission says, 'The first enfeoffment must be made ancestor.'

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『德高可宗，故號高宗。』

translations.literal: The Documents say, 'When virtue is lofty one may be honored—hence the title High Exemplar.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, 'When virtue is lofty one may be honored—hence the title High Exemplar.'

sentences.zh: 今宜本三代之定制，去魏、晉之亂法，守貞觀、開元之憲章，而擬議大名，垂以為訓。

translations.literal: Now we should follow the fixed institutions of the Three Dynasties, discard the chaotic methods of Wei and Jin, keep the statutes of Zhenguan and Kaiyuan, and in proposing the great name hand it down as instruction.
translations.idiomatic: We should follow the Three Dynasties, discard Wei and Jin's confusion, keep the charters of Zhenguan and Kaiyuan, and in choosing the great title set a teaching for posterity.

sentences.zh: 大行廟號，宜稱宗。」

translations.literal: The temple title of the late emperor should be Exemplar."
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's temple title should be Exemplar."

sentences.zh: 制從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 故事，祔廟之禮，先告於太極殿，然後奉神主赴太廟。

translations.literal: By precedent, in the rite of enshrining in the ancestral temple, one first announces at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, then conveys the spirit tablet to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, before enshrining in the ancestral temple one announces at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, then conveys the spirit tablet to the temple.

sentences.zh: 祔禮畢，不再告於太極殿。

translations.literal: When the enshrinement rite was complete, one did not again announce at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: When enshrinement was complete, one did not announce again at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 時憲宗祔廟禮畢，執政詳舊典，令有司再告祔享禮畢於太極殿。

translations.literal: At that time, when Xianzong's enshrinement rite was complete, those in power examined the old canon and ordered the responsible offices to announce again at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate that the enshrinement and offering rite was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong's enshrinement was complete, those in power examined precedent and ordered a second announcement at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate that enshrinement and offering were finished.

sentences.zh: 彥威執議以為不可，執政怒。

translations.literal: Yanwei argued that this was improper; those in power were angry.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei argued this was improper; those in power were angry.

sentences.zh: 會宗正寺進祝版，誤以憲宗為睿宗。

translations.literal: When the Court of Imperial Clan presented the prayer boards, they mistakenly wrote Xianzong for Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Court of Imperial Clan presented the prayer boards, they mistakenly wrote Ruizong for Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 執政銜其強，奏祝版參差，博士之罪，彥威坐削一階，奪兩季俸。

translations.literal: Those in power, resenting his stubbornness, memorialized that the prayer boards were inconsistent and that the erudites were at fault; Yanwei was demoted one rank and lost two seasons' salary.
translations.idiomatic: Resenting his stubbornness, they memorialized that the prayer boards were inconsistent and blamed the erudites; Yanwei was demoted one rank and forfeited two seasons' salary.

sentences.zh: 彥威殊不低回，每議禮事，守正不阿附，君子稱之。

translations.literal: Yanwei was not at all abashed; whenever he deliberated on ritual matters he upheld rectitude and would not curry favor; gentlemen praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei was unbowed; in every ritual debate he stood upright without flattery; gentlemen praised him.

sentences.zh: 累轉司封員外郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted successively to Vice Director and Director in the Bureau of Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director and director in the bureau of enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 弘文館舊不置學士，文宗特置一員以待彥威。

translations.literal: The Hongwen Hall had not previously had an academician; Emperor Wenzong specially established one post for Yanwei.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwen Hall had had no academician; Emperor Wenzong specially created one post for Yanwei.

sentences.zh: 尋使魏博宣慰，特賜金紫。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent as envoy to pacify Weibo and was specially granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent to pacify Weibo and was specially granted gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to remonstrance grandee.

sentences.zh: 朝廷自誅李師道，收復淄青十二州，未定戶籍。

translations.literal: After the court executed Li Shidao and recovered the twelve prefectures of Ziqing, household registers were not yet fixed.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shidao was executed and the twelve Ziqing prefectures recovered, household registers were unsettled.

sentences.zh: 乃命彥威充十二州勘定兩稅使。

translations.literal: Yanwei was ordered to serve as Commissioner for Fixing the Two-Tax System in the Twelve Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei was ordered to serve as commissioner for fixing the two-tax system in the twelve prefectures.

sentences.zh: 朝法振舉，人不以為煩。

translations.literal: Court law was vigorously enforced, and the people did not find it burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: Court law was vigorously enforced without burdening the people.

sentences.zh: 以本官兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: In his original post he was concurrently Compiler of the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently compiler at the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 彥威通悉典故，宿儒碩學皆讓之。

translations.literal: Yanwei was thoroughly versed in precedents; veteran scholars yielded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei knew precedents thoroughly; senior scholars deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 時以僕射上事儀註，前後不定，中丞李漢奏定，朝議未以為允。

translations.literal: At that time the protocol for vice ministers attending to business was unsettled before and after; Vice Censor Li Han memorialized to fix it, but court opinion did not consider it acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: At that time protocol for vice ministers conducting business had long been unsettled; Vice Censor Li Han memorialized to fix it, but opinion was unsatisfied.

sentences.zh: 中書門下奏請依元和七年已前儀註，左右僕射上日，請受諸司四品六品丞郎已下拜。

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized requesting that protocol before the seventh year of Yuanhe be followed: on the day the Left and Right Vice Ministers took office, subordinates of the fourth and sixth ranks and directors and vice directors should bow.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat petitioned to follow protocol before the seventh year of Yuanhe: on the day left and right vice ministers took office, subordinates through the fourth and sixth ranks and directors and vice directors should bow.

sentences.zh: 彥威奏論曰：「臣謹按《開元禮》：凡受冊官，並與卑官答拜。

translations.literal: Yanwei memorialized in argument, "Your servant respectfully notes the 'Kaiyuan Rites': all officials receiving appointment documents also return bows to lower officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei argued in a memorial: "I respectfully note the Kaiyuan Rites: all officials receiving appointment documents also return bows to lower officials.

sentences.zh: 國朝官品，令三師三公正一品，尚書令正二品，並是冊拜授官。

translations.literal: In our dynasty's official ranks, the Three Dukes and Three Masters are of the first rank, and the Director of the Secretariat is of the second rank—all are offices conferred by appointment documents.
translations.idiomatic: In our ranks the three dukes and three masters are first rank and the director of the secretariat second rank—all offices conferred by appointment edict.

sentences.zh: 上之日，亦無受朝官再拜之文。

translations.literal: On the day of assumption there is no text of court officials bowing again.
translations.idiomatic: On assumption day there is no provision for court officials to bow again.

sentences.zh: 僕射班次三公，又是尚書令副貳之職，雖端揆之重，有異百寮，然與群官比肩事主。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister ranks with the Three Dukes and is also deputy to the Director of the Secretariat; though the weight of chief minister differs from the hundred officials, he nonetheless stands shoulder to shoulder with the multitude in serving his lord.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister ranks with the three dukes and is deputy to the director; though heavier than the hundred officials, he still serves the throne alongside them.

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰『非其臣即答拜之』。

translations.literal: The Rites say, 'If he is not his minister, then return the bow.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say, 'If he is not his minister, then return the bow.'

sentences.zh: 又曰『大夫之臣不稽首』。

translations.literal: It also says, 'The great officer's servants do not perform the forehead-to-ground bow.'
translations.idiomatic: It also says, 'A great officer's servants do not perform the forehead bow.'

sentences.zh: 非尊家臣，以避君也。

translations.literal: This is not to honor household servants but to avoid the lord.
translations.idiomatic: This is not to honor house servants but to avoid the lord.

sentences.zh: 即僕射上日受常參官拜，事頗非儀。

translations.literal: Thus for the vice minister on assumption day to receive bows from regularly attending officials is quite contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: For a vice minister on assumption day to receive bows from regularly attending officials is quite unritual.

sentences.zh: 況元和七年已經奏議，酌為定制，編在國章。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the seventh year of Yuanhe this was already deliberated and set as fixed regulation, compiled in the national statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the seventh year of Yuanhe this was already deliberated and fixed in the national statutes.

sentences.zh: 近年上儀，又有受拜之禮，禮文乍變，物論未安，請依元和七年敕為定。」

translations.literal: In recent years the assumption protocol again includes receiving bows; the ritual text has suddenly changed and public opinion is unsettled—please fix it according to the edict of the seventh year of Yuanhe."
translations.idiomatic: Recently assumption protocol again includes receiving bows; ritual has suddenly changed and opinion is uneasy—please fix it by the seventh-year edict."

sentences.zh: 時李程為左僕射，宰執難於改革，雖不從其議，論者稱之。

translations.literal: At that time Li Cheng was Left Vice Minister; the chief ministers found reform difficult and though they did not follow his argument, commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng was then left vice minister; the chief ministers found reform awkward and though they did not accept his view, commentators praised him.

sentences.zh: 興平縣人上官興，因醉殺人亡竄，吏執其父下獄，興自首請罪，以出其父。

translations.literal: Shangguan Xing of Xingping County, drunk, killed a man and fled; the officers arrested his father and imprisoned him; Xing surrendered himself to answer for the crime in order to release his father.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Xing of Xingping, drunk, killed a man and fled; officers arrested his father; Xing surrendered to free his father.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹杜悰、御史中丞宇文鼎，以其首罪免父，有光孝義，請減死配流。

translations.literal: Magistrate of the Capital District Du Cong and Vice Censor Yuwen Ding, because he confessed to the capital crime to free his father and thereby displayed filial righteousness, asked that death be reduced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Magistrate Du Cong and Vice Censor Yuwen Ding, because Xing confessed to the capital crime to free his father and displayed filial duty, asked that death be reduced to exile.

sentences.zh: 彥威與諫官上言曰：「殺人者死，百王共守。

translations.literal: Yanwei and the remonstrance officials memorialized, "He who kills shall die—this the hundred kings jointly uphold.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei and the remonstrance officials memorialized: "He who kills shall die—all kings uphold this.

sentences.zh: 若許殺人不死，是教殺人。

translations.literal: If we permit killers not to die, we teach killing.
translations.idiomatic: If killers need not die, we teach killing.

sentences.zh: 興雖免父，不合減死。」

translations.literal: Though Xing freed his father, he should not have his death reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Though Xing freed his father, his death should not be reduced."

sentences.zh: 詔竟許決流。

translations.literal: An edict nevertheless permitted exile after execution.
translations.idiomatic: An edict nevertheless permitted exile after sentencing.

sentences.zh: 彥威詣中書投宰相面論，語訐氣盛。

translations.literal: Yanwei went to the Secretariat and argued face to face with the chief ministers; his words were cutting and his manner overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei went to the secretariat and argued face to face with the chief ministers, his words sharp and his manner overbearing.

sentences.zh: 執政怒，左授河南少尹。

translations.literal: Those in power were angry and demoted him to Vice Magistrate of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power were angry and demoted him to vice magistrate of Henan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改司農卿。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made minister of the court of the imperial granaries.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔重之。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 既秉政，授青州刺史、兼御史大夫，充平盧軍節度、淄青等觀察使。

translations.literal: Once he held power he appointed Yanwei Prefect of Qing Prefecture, concurrently Chief Censor, Military Commissioner of Pinglu Army, and Observation Commissioner of Ziqing.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power Li Zongmin made Yanwei prefect of Qing, concurrent chief censor, military commissioner of Pinglu, and observation commissioner of Ziqing.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，召拜戶部侍郎，尋判度支。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng he was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue and soon directed the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaicheng he was summoned as vice minister of revenue and soon directed the department of revenue.

sentences.zh: 彥威儒學雖優，亦勤吏事，然貨泉之柄，素非所長，性既剛訐，自恃有余。

translations.literal: Though Yanwei's Confucian learning was excellent, he was also diligent in administrative affairs; yet the handle of currency had never been his strength, and his nature was blunt and contentious, trusting in his own surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yanwei's scholarship was excellent and he was diligent in office, finance had never been his strength; he was blunt and contentious, confident in his own sufficiency.

sentences.zh: 嘗紫宸廷奏曰：「臣自計司按見管錢穀文簿，皆量入以為出，使經費必足，無所刻削。

translations.literal: Once at an audience in the Purple Forbidden Hall he memorialized, "Your servant, reviewing the ledgers of money and grain under my charge, all measure output against input so that expenditures are sure to be sufficient, without any cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Once at audience in the Purple Forbidden Hall he said: "Reviewing the money and grain ledgers under my charge, I measure output against input so expenditures are always sufficient, without arbitrary cuts.

sentences.zh: 且百口之家，猶有歲蓄，而軍用錢物，一切通用，悉隨色額占定，終歲支給，無毫厘之差。

translations.literal: Even a household of a hundred mouths keeps yearly stores, yet military funds and goods are all in general use, each fixed by category and amount, paid out through the year without the slightest discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Even a household of a hundred keeps yearly stores; military funds are all in common use, fixed by category and amount, paid through the year without the slightest discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 倘臣一旦愚迷，欲自欺竊，亦不可得也。」

translations.literal: If your servant one day were foolish and wished to deceive and steal, it would also be impossible."
translations.idiomatic: If I one day wished to deceive and steal, it would still be impossible."

sentences.zh: 名曰《度支占額圖》。

translations.literal: It was titled "Chart of Revenue Quotas."
translations.idiomatic: He titled it Chart of Revenue Quotas.

sentences.zh: 既而又進《供軍圖》曰：「起至德、乾元之際，迄於永貞、元和之初，天下有觀察者十，節度二十有九，防禦者四，經略者三。

translations.literal: He then also presented the "Chart of Army Supply," saying, "From the time of Zhide and Qianyuan down to the beginning of Yongzhen and Yuanhe, throughout the realm there were ten observation commissioners, twenty-nine military commissioners, four defenders, and three pacification commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented the Chart of Army Supply, saying: "From Zhide and Qianyuan to the beginning of Yongzhen and Yuanhe, the realm had ten observation commissioners, twenty-nine military commissioners, four defenders, and three pacification commissioners.

sentences.zh: 掎角之師，犬牙相制，大都通邑，無不有兵，都計中外各額，至八十余萬。

translations.literal: Armies at mutual angles, like dogs' teeth interlocking—great thoroughfares and walled cities all had troops; altogether the inner and outer quotas reached more than eight hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Forces interlocked like dogs' teeth; every great road and walled city had troops; inner and outer quotas totaled more than eight hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 長慶戶口凡三百三十五萬，而兵額約九十九萬，通計三戶資一兵。

translations.literal: In Changqing the registered households totaled three million three hundred fifty thousand, while military quotas were about nine hundred ninety thousand—altogether three households supporting one soldier.
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing registered households totaled 3,350,000 while military quotas were about 990,000—three households per soldier.

sentences.zh: 今計天下租賦，一歲所入，總不過三千五百余萬，而上供之數三之一焉。

translations.literal: Now counting the empire's land tax, what is collected in one year altogether does not exceed thirty-five million and more, while the amount sent upward is one third.
translations.idiomatic: Annual land tax collection does not exceed thirty-five million; the amount sent upward is one third.

sentences.zh: 三萬之中，二給衣賜。

translations.literal: Of the thirty-five million, two parts go to clothing and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Of that total, two parts go to clothing and rewards.

sentences.zh: 自留州留使兵士衣賜之外，其余四十萬眾，仰給度支。

translations.literal: Apart from clothing and rewards for troops retained by the prefectures and military commissioners, the remaining four hundred thousand depend on the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from clothing and rewards for troops retained locally, the remaining four hundred thousand depend on the department of revenue.

sentences.zh: 伏以時逢理安，運屬神聖，然而兵不可弭，食哉惟時。

translations.literal: We submit that though the times meet with ordered rule and the fortune belongs to the sacred ruler, yet troops cannot be disbanded and food is always timely.
translations.idiomatic: Though the age meets ordered rule and fortune rests with a sacred ruler, troops cannot be disbanded and food is ever urgent.

sentences.zh: 憂勤之端，兵食是切。

translations.literal: At the root of anxious diligence, troops and provisions are foremost.
translations.idiomatic: At the root of anxious toil, troops and provisions are foremost.

sentences.zh: 臣謬司邦計，虔奉睿圖，輒纂事功，庶裨聖覽。」

translations.literal: Your servant, wrongly holding the state's accounts, reverently serving the sage design, has compiled achievements in hope of aiding the imperial view."
translations.idiomatic: Wrongly holding the state's accounts, I reverently serve the sage design and compile this in hope of aiding the imperial view."

sentences.zh: 又纂集國初已來至貞元帝代功臣，如《左氏傳》體敘事，號曰《唐典》，進之。

translations.literal: He also compiled meritorious ministers from the founding of the dynasty to the era of Emperor Zhenyuan, narrating events in the manner of the 'Zuo Tradition,' titled "Tang Canon," and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled meritorious ministers from the founding through the Zhenyuan era in Zuo Tradition style as Tang Canon and presented it.

sentences.zh: 彥威既掌利權，心希大用。

translations.literal: Yanwei, now holding the lever of profit, inwardly hoped for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: Now holding the lever of profit, Yanwei inwardly hoped for high office.

sentences.zh: 時內官仇士良、魚弘誌禁中用事。

translations.literal: At that time the inner attendants Qiu Shiliang and Yu Hongzhi wielded power within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time inner attendants Qiu Shiliang and Yu Hongzhi wielded power in the palace.

sentences.zh: 先是左右神策軍多以所賜衣物於度支中估，判使多曲從，厚給其價。

translations.literal: Earlier the Left and Right Shence Armies often had gifted clothing appraised at the Department of Revenue, and the acting commissioner mostly yielded and gave a generous price.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the left and right Shence armies often had gifted clothing appraised at the department of revenue; acting commissioners mostly yielded generous prices.

sentences.zh: 開成初，有詔禁止，然趨利者猶希意從其請托。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng there was an edict forbidding this, yet those seeking profit still hoped to please and granted their requests.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaicheng an edict forbade this, yet profiteers still pleased them and granted requests.

sentences.zh: 至是，彥威大結私恩，凡內官請托，無不如意，物議鄙其躁妄。

translations.literal: Now Yanwei greatly cultivated private favor; whatever inner attendants requested was as they wished; public opinion despised his rash presumption.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yanwei cultivated private favor lavishly; whatever inner attendants asked he granted; opinion despised his rashness.

sentences.zh: 復修王播舊事，貢奉羨余，殆無虛日。

translations.literal: He again revived Wang Bo's old practice, presenting surplus tribute almost every day.
translations.idiomatic: He revived Wang Bo's old practice, presenting surplus tribute almost daily.

sentences.zh: 會邊軍上訴衣賜不時，兼之朽故。

translations.literal: When frontier troops complained that clothing and rewards were not timely and were moreover rotten,
translations.idiomatic: When frontier troops complained that clothing and rewards came late and were rotten,

sentences.zh: 宰臣惡其所為，令攝度支人吏付臺推訊。

translations.literal: the chief ministers hated his conduct and ordered the revenue clerks taken over by the Censorate for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: the chief ministers hated his conduct and handed his revenue clerks to the censorate for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 彥威略不介懷，入司視事。

translations.literal: Yanwei was not concerned at all and entered the office to conduct business.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei was unconcerned and entered the office to work.

sentences.zh: 及人吏受罰，左授衛尉卿，停務，方還私第。

translations.literal: When the clerks were punished he was demoted to Minister of the Imperial Guard, suspended from duties, and only then returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the clerks were punished he was demoted to minister of the imperial guard, suspended, and only then went home.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，檢校禮部尚書，代殷侑為許州刺史，充忠武軍節度、陳許溵觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year he was made Acting Minister of Rites, replacing Yin You as Prefect of Xu Prefecture and Military Commissioner of Zhongwu Army and Observation Commissioner of Chen, Xu, and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year he was made acting minister of rites, replacing Yin You as prefect of Xu, military commissioner of Zhongwu, and observation commissioner of Chen, Xu, and Wen.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，入為兵部侍郎，歷方鎮，檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era he entered court as Vice Minister of War and served in outer commands as Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huichang era he entered court as vice minister of war and served in outer commands as acting minister of war.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈僕射，謚曰靖。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Vice Minister with the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made vice minister with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 【贊】=史臣曰：世以治軍戎，決權變，非儒者之事。

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historians say: The world holds that governing armies, deciding expedients, and wielding authority are not the affairs of Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historians say: The world holds that governing armies, deciding expedients, and wielding authority are not the affairs of Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 而王翃、郗士美釋縫掖之儒衣，奮將軍之旗鼓，俾士赴湯火，威振籓籬，何其壯也！

translations.literal: Yet Wang Hong and Chi Shimei put off the scholar's robe, raised the general's banners and drums, made soldiers rush into fire and water, and shook prestige along the frontier—how magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Hong and Chi Shimei put off the scholar's robe, raised the general's banners and drums, sent men into fire and water, and shook prestige along the frontier—how magnificent!

sentences.zh: 所謂非秦無人，吾謀適不用也。

translations.literal: The saying goes, 'If not for Qin, there would be no man in Qin'—our stratagem just happened not to be used.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, 'If not for Qin, there would be no man in Qin'—our stratagem just happened not to be used.

sentences.zh: 二子遭遇英主，伸其效用，宜哉！

translations.literal: The two men encountered enlightened rulers, extended their usefulness—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The two men met enlightened rulers and gave full play to their talents—fitting indeed!

sentences.zh: 李建侯不屈於賊庭，馬會元見伸於貝錦，臨危挺操，所謂貞臣，將相之榮，固其宜矣。

translations.literal: Li Jianhou did not bend in the rebel court; Ma Huiyuan showed himself amid slanderous brocade; facing peril they upheld integrity—the so-called loyal ministers; the glory of minister and general was surely their due.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jianhou did not bend in the rebel court; Ma Huiyuan showed himself amid slanderous brocade; facing peril they upheld integrity—true loyal ministers; ministerial and general glory was surely their due.

sentences.zh: 辛潞州之特達，韋僕射之峻整，王尚書之果敢，皆一時之偉器也。

translations.literal: Xin of Luzhou's exceptional attainment, Vice Minister Wei's stern rectitude, and Minister Wang's bold decisiveness were all great vessels of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Xin of Luzhou's exceptional attainment, Vice Minister Wei's stern rectitude, and Minister Wang's bold decisiveness were all great vessels of the age.

sentences.zh: 若以道自牧，求福不回，即能臣也。

translations.literal: If they had cultivated themselves by the Way, sought blessing without turning aside, they could have been able ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Had they cultivated themselves by the Way and sought blessing without turning aside, they could have been able ministers.

sentences.zh: 而彥威欲為巧宦，不亦疏乎？

translations.literal: Yet Yanwei wished to be a clever office-seeker—is he not shallow?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yanwei wished to be a clever office-seeker—is he not shallow?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：見危致命，臨難不恐。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Meeting peril they gave their lives; facing hardship they did not fear.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Meeting peril they gave their lives; facing hardship they did not fear.

sentences.zh: 士美、建侯，仁者之勇。

translations.literal: Shimei and Jianhou—the courage of the benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei and Jianhou—the courage of the benevolent.

sentences.zh: 弘景陸離，駁正黃扉。

translations.literal: Hongjing was varied and brilliant, correcting the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing was varied and brilliant, correcting the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 貪名喪道，狂哉彥威。

translations.literal: Greedy for fame and losing the Way—how reckless, Yanwei!
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for fame and losing the Way—how reckless, Yanwei!
